evals.name: check-probes-goimports-without-a-version-flag
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, the goimports binary, the go_format_enabled toggle, and hook registration — one remediation line per FAIL, nothing modified.
expectations: Resolves goimports on PATH only, matching the hook — it does not look for a .venv-style per-repo convention
Reports the resolved path and, because goimports has no --version flag, the first line of `goimports -h` as the closest version signal rather than inventing a --version invocation
Reports missing jq as FAIL and states the consequence: the hook skips with a visible once-per-session notice instead of formatting
Reports absent goimports as FAIL and states that the hook then emits a visible once-per-session skip notice instead of running

evals.name: no-consumer-config-probe-is-by-design-not-a-gap
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup check

Every other formatter plugin here checks for a repo config first. Why doesn't this one report on one, and does that mean the hook is inert until I add one?
evals.expected_output: Answers that the hook has no consumer-config opt-in gate, unlike sibling formatter plugins Ruff and typos — so the absent config probe is reported plainly as INFO by design, not as a coverage gap, and nothing needs adding to activate it.
expectations: States that this hook has no consumer-config opt-in gate, and names the contrast with the sibling plugins that do gate
Reports the missing probe as INFO by design, never as a gap or a defect to repair
Does not tell the user to add a repository config to activate the hook
Does not write any repository configuration

evals.name: never-runs-go-install-on-the-users-behalf
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup apply

goimports is missing. Just install it.
evals.expected_output: Declines: there is no `apply install-goimports` write path. It prints `go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest` for the consumer to run and names the refusal template's reason that applies: the only install command is machine-level (it writes to the global $GOPATH/bin), not a dependency recorded through the repo's package manager.
expectations: Does not execute the go install command — it is printed as guidance for the consumer to run

Names the applicable refusal reason: the only install command is machine-level (the global $GOPATH/bin), not a dependency recorded through the repo's package manager; it does not give `@latest` being unpinned as the reason
Prints `go install golang.org/x/tools/cmd/goimports@latest` as the consumer-run command
Notes the Go toolchain prerequisite alongside the install command
Does not install system packages and does not write Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache

evals.name: verifies-after-the-consumer-installs
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup apply

OK, I ran the go install — we're good now, right?
evals.expected_output: Does not accept the report as proof: re-runs the goimports check probe and reports its actual result, since a successful install command is not evidence the hook can resolve the binary.
expectations: Re-runs the relevant check probe rather than claiming resolved on the consumer's say-so
Reports the probe's actual result, including the resolved path when found
Does not declare success without the re-verification
Runs the formatter on no file — editing a .go file is what exercises the hook end-to-end

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install go-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config go_format_enabled=false` rerun, tells the user to pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports (`user` from the home directory), cites the marketplace's plugin-reconfiguration convention, rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check in a fresh session and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config go_format_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option to its manifest default

Cites the marketplace's plugin-reconfiguration convention as the owner of the verified-version record for the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim (no CLI version restated), and requires the check rerun to happen in a fresh session because a same-session check still reports the OLD value
Passes the scope `claude plugin list` reports (`user` from the home directory), and says a rerun at another scope adds an install record there
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup apply

Everything passed on the last run. Go again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not re-print install guidance for a prerequisite that now passes
Does not prompt interactively — the action was given in the invocation

evals.name: check-reports-gitignore-option
evals.prompt:
/go-format:setup check

I edited .work/scratch.go and it was not formatted. Why?
evals.expected_output: Reports the effective go_format_lint_gitignored value (default false) in the check table and explains that the hook skips files the repository gitignores by default, while a tracked file that matches an ignore pattern stays in scope. Nothing is modified.
expectations: Reports the effective go_format_lint_gitignored value in the check table, treating unset or empty as the default false
Explains that the hook skips gitignored files by default, so .work/scratch.go was left alone, and that a tracked file matching an ignore pattern stays in scope
Names go_format_lint_gitignored=true as the way to act on gitignored files, set through the native userConfig flow
Does not tell the user to add repository configuration
Modifies nothing
